title: The same purpose added back budget after budget
question: Which purposes return to the Board’s list in later years instead of entering the regular budget?
finding: At least 35 purposes appear in two or more of the thirteen lists (6 in three), worth $19.1 million in first-year money; 3 carried a one-time mark in one of those years. The largest is “Expansion of the Code Enforcement Outreach program”, $5.5 million across 2014, 2023, 2024.
how: First-year lines are grouped when they sit in the same department, carry the same district (or none) and share at least 60% of the distinctive words in a title of three or more such words. A group is listed when it spans two or more budgets. Lines the scans garbled are left out.
limits: This is a floor, not a count: wording changes from year to year, departments are renamed and five lists are scans, so most repeats are missed. Read the two wordings shown before treating a row as one program. It shows a program living outside the base budget, renewed by negotiation each June.
